sentences.ko: 응, 솔직히 지금은 다들 좀 없었으면 좋겠어.
sentences.text: Yeah, I'm kind of wishing everyone wasn't here right now.

alts.text: Honestly, I kinda wish it was just us right now.
To be honest, I would rather that everyone were not here at the moment.

sentences.note: **kind of wishing** 는 '좀 ~했으면 싶다'를 부드럽게 돌려 말할 때 씁니다. 대놓고 '다들 가 줘'라고 하기 어려운 자리에서 속마음을 슬쩍 털어놓는 말투예요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그러니까 내가 노래 부르다 중간에 재채기해도 일부러 그러는 거 아니야.
sentences.text: So if I sneeze in the middle of a song, it's not on purpose.

alts.text: Heads up, if I sneeze mid-song, I don't mean it.
Please understand that if I sneeze during a song, it will not be intentional.

sentences.note: **on purpose** 는 '일부러'로, 오해받기 전에 미리 '고의 아니야'라고 해 둘 때 딱 맞습니다. **in the middle of** 는 '~하는 도중에'라는 뜻으로 일상에서 아주 자주 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: So, I am just going to leave it entirely up to the gods of fate.

alts.text: Eh, I'll just let fate decide.
I will simply leave the decision entirely to fate.

sentences.note: **leave it entirely up to** 는 '전적으로 ~에게 맡기다'입니다. 고민하다 손을 놓을 때 'gods of fate' 처럼 과장해서 붙이면 농담 섞인 말투가 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그래서, 그 여자 진짜 또 만날 거야?
sentences.text: So, are you actually going to see her again?

alts.text: Wait, you're seriously seeing her again?
Do you really intend to see her again?

sentences.note: **actually** 는 '설마 진짜로?'라는 놀람이나 확인을 담습니다. 친구가 소개팅 상대 얘기를 할 때 이렇게 되묻는 게 자연스러워요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.text: I did the windows, I did the floors.

alts.text: Windows, floors — did 'em both.
I cleaned the windows, and I cleaned the floors as well.

sentences.note: **did the windows** 처럼 do 뒤에 집안의 장소나 물건을 붙이면 '그걸 청소했다'는 뜻이 됩니다. do the dishes(설거지), do the laundry(빨래)와 같은 쓰임으로, 집안일 얘기할 때 clean 대신 흔히 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 솔직히 나 좀 너무 편해진 것 같아.
sentences.text: In fact, I think I might be a little too comfortable.

alts.text: Honestly, I'm maybe a bit too comfy.
As a matter of fact, I believe I may be somewhat too comfortable.

sentences.note: **a little too comfortable** 는 소파에 너무 오래 늘어져 있을 때나 지금 상황에 너무 익숙해져서 긴장이 풀렸을 때 농담처럼 하는 말입니다. **In fact** 는 앞에서 한 말보다 한 발 더 나갈 때 붙입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.text: Why don't we just let the machine get that?

alts.text: Just let it go to voicemail.
Perhaps we should allow the answering machine to take the call.

sentences.note: 전화가 울릴 때 **get that** 은 '그 전화 받다'라는 뜻입니다. 요즘은 받기 싫은 전화가 오면 **let it go to voicemail** 이라고 많이 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 왜 거길 볼 생각을 못 했지?
sentences.text: I don't know why we didn't think to check there.

alts.text: Can't believe we never checked there.
I do not understand why it did not occur to us to look there.

sentences.note: **think to** 는 '~할 생각이 나다'라는 뜻이라, 잃어버린 물건을 뻔한 자리에서 찾았을 때 딱 맞는 말입니다. 격식 있게는 **it did not occur to us** 라고 합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.text: All right, who you got it narrowed down to?

alts.text: So who's on your shortlist?
Which candidates have you narrowed it down to?

sentences.note: **narrowed down** 은 여러 개 중에서 몇 개로 '추리다'라는 뜻으로, 사람·집·선물을 고르는 중인 친구에게 묻기 좋습니다. **shortlist** 는 마지막까지 남은 후보 목록입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.text: Where'd you get fruit at 4 in the morning?

alts.text: You found fruit at 4 a.m.?
How were you able to find fruit at four o'clock in the morning?

sentences.note: **Where'd you get** 는 Where did you get 을 줄인 말로, 친구가 뜻밖의 물건을 들고 있을 때 바로 튀어나오는 질문입니다. 새벽 시간은 **4 in the morning** 처럼 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends
